name: An inferred mason's household (south division)
head: inf_mason_south_02

arrival.note: NOT AN ARRIVAL, A BOUND. Nothing dates a hypothesised household, and a year would be a claim nobody made. `not_later_than` the scene date states the only thing the inference carries: the town's need is measured on 1 July 1835, so the household is posited as being here by then and at no stated time before it.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not claimed. The layer infers households, not families: the person entries here are the ones the trade argument requires and nothing counts wives or children, because counting them would multiply a hypothesis by an invention.

origin.note: Not claimed. Where a hypothesised resident came from is unknowable by construction, and the documented layer's origins (Vermont, Washington, Ann Arbor) are evidence about those men and not a distribution to sample from.

reason_for_coming.note: Not claimed for the person. The reason the HOUSEHOLD is in the dataset is the trade argument in research_note, which is a statement about the town and not about a motive.

lives_at.note: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d4_006 is an anonymous inferred roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.

works_at.note: NO SEPARATE WORKPLACE. A mason in this town worked in other people's buildings, in the street, or in the dwelling itself, and inventing a shop for the sake of a link would be inventing a building.

present_on_scene_date.note: Presence on the scene date IS the hypothesis: this household exists in the dataset because the town of 1 July 1835 demonstrably needed households of this trade. It is not a finding about anybody's whereabouts.

persons.name: A mason (inferred resident, unnamed)

occupation.note: EVERY FRAME HOUSE IN THE TOWN CARRIES A HEARTH AND A STACK. Blodgett's yard on the north side has made brick since the spring of 1833 (Andreas, scan p. 1161), and the most ambitious building under way on the scene date - the Lake House - is going up in brick in a town otherwise built of logs and boards. The documented layer holds one mason. Three more mason households are inferred: the chimney trade alone, at 398 dwellings, is more work than one man's.

persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. The name field carries a designation because inventing a surname would make this record indistinguishable at a glance from the documented layer beside it. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). research_note: INFERRED HOUSEHOLD - second of 4 mason households in this layer, in the south division. EVERY FRAME HOUSE IN THE TOWN CARRIES A HEARTH AND A STACK. Blodgett's yard on the north side has made brick since the spring of 1833 (Andreas, scan p. 1161), and the most ambitious building under way on the scene date - the Lake House - is going up in brick in a town otherwise built of logs and boards. The documented layer holds one mason. Three more mason households are inferred: the chimney trade alone, at 398 dwellings, is more work than one man's. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
